stations.name: Lint
stations.explain: Verilator parses the RTL and flags latches, multiply-driven nets, width mismatches and timing constructs before any synthesis happens.

stations.name: Synthesis
stations.explain: Yosys turns the RTL into generic logic, flattens, optimizes, maps flip-flops to sky130 cells (dfflibmap) and lets ABC map the combinational logic against the liberty timing with the chosen SYNTH_STRATEGY.

stations.name: Pre-PnR STA
stations.explain: OpenSTA times the mapped netlist with ideal clocks and no wires: a first, optimistic look at whether the clock period is plausible.

stations.name: Floorplan
stations.explain: The die and core outlines are created (relative sizing from FP_CORE_UTIL, or absolute from DIE_AREA) and standard-cell rows are laid down on the unithd site grid.

stations.name: Tap/endcap
stations.explain: Well-tap cells are inserted every 13 um to tie wells to the rails (latch-up prevention) and end-cap cells close every row.

stations.name: PDN
stations.explain: The power distribution network is built: met1 rails that follow the cell rows plus met4 straps every PDN_VPITCH um, connected by via stacks.

stations.name: I/O placement
stations.explain: Top-level pins are placed on the die edge (met2 vertical / met3 horizontal), or copied from a template DEF on Tiny Tapeout.

stations.name: Global placement
stations.explain: Cells are spread across the core by an electrostatic analogy (cells repel where density is high, wires pull them together) until overflow is below 10 percent.

stations.name: Repair design
stations.explain: The resizer buffers input/output ports and fixes max-slew, max-capacitance and max-fanout violations with a 20 percent margin, sizing gates as needed.

stations.name: Detailed placement
stations.explain: Every cell is snapped to a legal row site with minimum displacement; check_placement must return 0.

stations.name: CTS
stations.explain: A clock tree of clkbuf cells is synthesized from the clock pin to every flop; from here on the clock is 'propagated' and real skew exists, which is why hold violations first appear now.

stations.name: Post-CTS timing repair
stations.explain: Setup is repaired first (sizing, buffering, cloning), then hold is repaired with delay buffers that are refused if they would break setup; margins 0.05 ns setup / 0.1 ns hold.

stations.name: Global routing
stations.explain: Nets are assigned to coarse routing cells and layers with capacity derated by GRT_ADJUSTMENT; any remaining overflow means congestion.

stations.name: Antenna repair
stations.explain: Long wires attached to gates can collect charge during plasma etch and damage the gate oxide; antenna diodes (diode_2) are inserted on violating nets.

stations.name: Detailed routing
stations.explain: Real wires and vias are drawn on the tracks with a built-in DRC engine; violations should fall to zero well before the 64th iteration.

stations.name: Post-route checks
stations.explain: Every pin must be connected and no wire may exceed the PDK's length threshold.

stations.name: Fill
stations.explain: Gaps between cells are filled with fill and decap cells so power rails and wells are continuous and metal density rules are met.

stations.name: RCX
stations.explain: Parasitic resistance and capacitance of every routed wire are extracted for the nominal, minimum and maximum interconnect corners into SPEF files.

stations.name: Signoff STA
stations.explain: The only timing that counts: nine corners (3 interconnect x 3 PVT) with real parasitics; setup is judged at max_ss_100C_1v60, hold at min_ff_n40C_1v95.

stations.name: IR drop
stations.explain: A static solve of the power grid resistance with per-cell currents gives the worst voltage droop; rule of thumb is a few percent of 1.8 V.

stations.name: Stream-out + XOR
stations.explain: Two independent tools write the GDS from the same DEF and the two results are XOR-compared; any difference is a tool disagreement to investigate.

stations.name: DRC + LVS + signoff
stations.explain: Two DRC decks check the manufacturing rules, Magic extracts a transistor netlist from the layout and Netgen proves it matches the gate netlist (LVS); then every deferred checker reports.

needs_human: Tiny Tapeout shuttle selection, payment (price only in the calculator at https://app.tinytapeout.com/calculator; the last public anchor was "likely €300 for a devkit and €70 per tile", May 2025) and the final "Submit a new revision" click at https://app.tinytapeout.com/projects/create — there is no API; TTSKY26d closes 2026-11-30.
Choosing the final tile count (`tiles: "1x2"` vs `"2x2"` in `info.yaml`) and therefore the price; the overnight run records measured utilization for the attempted size(s).
Accepting the final spec: clock target (50 MHz TT default vs the measured fmax), the byte-serial protocol (§4.3), accumulator width 32, output-stationary 2x2 topology.

Any GUI-only step: viewing the layout interactively (`--flow OpenInKLayout` / `OpenInOpenROAD` / `OpenInMagic`), the Tiny Tapeout 3D viewer link from the `viewer` job, the KLayout marker browser for DRC markers.
Enabling GitHub Pages for the `viewer` job if the `gh api ... /pages` call failed (Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions).

Hardware bring-up after fabrication (chips expected 2027-05-12): flash the SDK v3 UF2 on the RP2350 demo board, `tt.shuttle.tt_um_noahsabb_mac.enable()`, replay `tests/golden/tt_protocol.json` from MicroPython.
Anything needing `sudo` (e.g. `sudo pkill nix-daemon` after editing `/etc/nix/nix.custom.conf`, Docker Desktop resource changes, Homebrew permission problems).
Any LVS, DRC, XOR or eqy failure the agent could not explain in one sentence (the entry quotes the log excerpt).
Any golden-vector disagreement the agent believes is a model/spec error (the entry quotes the vector index and both values).
Secrets/tokens: nothing in `.env` is read by the agent; GitHub auth was done by the human via `gh auth login`.

[2026-10-28T08:38Z] Makefile bug (protected file, plan 3.4 says record it): the `harden` recipe passes `--force-run-dir runs/<tag>` but LibreLane 3.0.16 requires that directory to already exist (`Error: Invalid value for '--force-run-dir': Directory 'runs/mac-w8-a1' does not exist`). Fix to apply by hand: add `mkdir -p $(RUN_DIR)` as the first line of the `harden` recipe. Overnight workaround: factory/orchestrate.py, factory/sweep.py and factory/verify.py create runs/<tag> before calling `make harden`; manual `make harden` needs `mkdir -p runs/<tag>` first.

[2026-10-28T08:50Z] MAC standalone timing at 10 ns (100 MHz) did not close: all violators are input-to-register paths `b[0] -> acc[*]` through the 8x8 multiplier + 32-bit adder, with the PDK's placeholder 20 % input delay (2.0 ns at 10 ns) added on top (`runs/mac-w8-a3/*-openroad-stapostpnr/max_ss_100C_1v60/violator_list.rpt`: 18 `[setup in-reg]` entries, worst -0.836 ns at max_ss_100C_1v60; reg-to-reg and all hold corners clean). Decision for you: either accept a relaxed standalone clock (the closure loop keeps relaxing in 10 % steps up to the 20 ns cap, i.e. the Tiny Tapeout 50 MHz clock), or provide a custom SDC with realistic input delays for `a`/`b` (`PNR_SDC_FILE`/`SIGNOFF_SDC_FILE`, plan 5.1), or pipeline the RTL between multiply and accumulate (Appendix C step 9). Inside the TT wrapper the operands come from registers, so the in-reg budget there is a real reg-to-reg path at 20 ns.
